1.a: We work with the most difficult cases — when doctors where a patient lives say there are no options left. We carefully review every request and honestly assess what can be done. If we see a way forward, we look for specialized treatment and arrange medical transport.

2.q: What does it cost the patient?
2.a: First we review your case — this costs nothing. What follows depends on the specific situation: what is needed, where, and how. We talk about the options and terms honestly and openly once we understand your case. Write to us — we'll assess it.

3.a: It depends on the case — the patient's condition, the treatment needed, and the route. Some requests call for urgent action, others for careful preparation. We recommend reaching out as early as possible: the sooner we study the situation, the more options we can find.

4.a: We arrange the transport of patients, including those who need medical accompaniment during the journey. We tailor the route, method, and accompaniment to each case and to the person's condition. We discuss the details individually after assessing the request.

5.q: How can I support the foundation?
5.a: You can support our work with a donation — every contribution helps us take on new cases.

AboutPage.metaDescription: New Life Foundation is a charitable foundation that helps patients find specialised treatment when local options have run out.
AboutPage.title: Finding possibilities for the most difficult cases
AboutPage.p1: New Life Charitable Foundation helps patients in complex medical situations — when treatment where they live is no longer possible or has been exhausted. We look for specialized treatment at appropriate clinics and arrange medical transport, so that each patient can reach the place where they can truly be helped.
AboutPage.p2: The foundation was established in 2019 to bring together the experience and resources of a team that has worked in medicine since 2011. Over these years we have learned one thing: even when a situation seems hopeless, there is almost always at least one option that simply hasn't been explored yet.
AboutPage.p3: The foundation is led by Olesya Oleksandrivna — an emergency and air-ambulance physician. Every day she works with the most difficult medical cases, consistently finding solutions where others don't see them. This experience is the foundation of how we work.
AboutPage.p4: We approach every case the same way: we carefully study the medical situation, look for realistic treatment options, and honestly assess what is possible. We do not promise results we cannot guarantee, and we do not name timelines until we fully understand the picture.
AboutPage.p5: Experience shows that options exist more often than it seems at first. Our job is to find them.

HowWeWorkPage.metaDescription: The foundation's process, step by step: from first contact to organising treatment.
HowWeWorkPage.title: How we work
HowWeWorkPage.lead: The foundation's process, step by step.

1.title: Consultation
1.body: You tell us about your situation and share the medical documents. We help you make sense of it: if needed, we arrange to clarify, confirm, or review the diagnosis and get opinions from other specialists.

2.title: Finding treatment
2.body: We search for clinics and specialists experienced with this specific diagnosis — at home and abroad. We come back to you with concrete options.

3.title: Arranging transportation
3.body: Once the clinic is confirmed, we organize the journey. This includes critically ill patients: with medical escort en route when their condition requires it.

4.title: Ongoing support
4.body: We are with you all the way — from the first request until you arrive for treatment. After that, we stay in touch and, when support is needed, help in whatever way we can.

cta.title: Need help?
cta.body: Fill in the form on the contact page and we will get back to you.

story-1.title: Sviatoslav’s Story
story-1.mapTeaser: Sviatoslav’s road to treatment in Barcelona
story-1.excerpt: At 1.5 years old, Sviatoslav was diagnosed with a brainstem tumor — a rare and complex condition causing neurological and respiratory complications.

sections.heading: Diagnosis in Ukraine 💔
sections.body: At 1.5 years old, Sviatoslav was diagnosed with a brainstem tumor — a rare and complex condition causing neurological and respiratory complications. Ukrainian doctors saw no path to treatment: a biopsy was considered too risky due to the likelihood of bleeding and complications, and surgery was deemed impossible.

sections.heading: Searching for a clinic abroad
sections.body: The family turned to leading clinics in several countries — Israel, Turkey, Germany, Austria, Greece, and others. Every one declined: the complexity of Sviatoslav’s case exceeded what these clinics were prepared to take on.

sections.heading: A solution found ❤️‍🩹
sections.body: The search led the family to Olesia, who specializes in finding treatment options for complex cases. She took on the search, consulting leading doctors and clinics worldwide, and ultimately found a solution: Sant Joan de Déu Hospital in Barcelona — one of Europe’s leading pediatric medical centers — agreed to take on Sviatoslav’s case.

sections.heading: Transport
sections.body: Given the risks associated with a brainstem tumor, doctors deemed air travel dangerous. The decision was made to transport Sviatoslav by medical vehicle — from Dnipro to Barcelona, 3,550 km, a two-day journey. The boy, who required continuous oxygen support, was accompanied by his parents, Yevheniia and Oleksandr.

sections.heading: Arrival in Barcelona 💗
sections.body: Sviatoslav was admitted to Sant Joan de Déu Hospital. He underwent an MRI, ultrasound, and necessary tests, and his tracheostomy tube was replaced. A medical board determined the next steps — including a biopsy and comprehensive diagnostics — to decide on a course of treatment.

sections.heading: Now
sections.body: Sviatoslav remains under the care of doctors in Barcelona, receiving treatment that no other clinic the family approached was able to provide.

story-2.title: Mykyta’s Story
story-2.excerpt: Mykyta is 4 years old. His condition suddenly worsened, and after examinations the family received a diagnosis: a brainstem tumor.

sections.heading: Diagnosis 💔
sections.body:
Mykyta is 4 years old. His condition suddenly worsened, and after examinations the family received a diagnosis: a brainstem tumor.

On December 3, 2024, doctors diagnosed a benign tumor beneath the cerebellar tentorium, complicated by hydrocephalus and brain swelling.

Two surgeries followed: on December 10, 2024, a shunt was placed to manage the hydrocephalus; on December 24, 2024, the tumor was partially removed.

sections.heading: Current situation
sections.body:
The tumor’s complex location made full removal impossible in Ukraine. It continues to grow, with a risk of becoming malignant.

On December 26, 2024, bulbar and neurological complications — including loss of the cough reflex — required a tracheostomy. Mykyta is oxygen-dependent, relies on a ventilator, and needs an aspirator to clear his airways. Periodic drops in blood oxygen levels (SpO2) pose an ongoing threat to his life.

sections.heading: Seeking help ❤️‍🩹
sections.body: Time is critical — each day the tumor presses harder on the brain, worsening the swelling. In Ukraine, doctors can offer only symptomatic care. The family has found a specialized clinic abroad, experienced in complex cases and ready to take on Mykyta’s treatment.

sections.heading: A message from his parents 💗
sections.body: Mykyta’s parents hold onto hope for their son’s full recovery and are doing everything they can for his treatment.

story-3.title: Lyonichka’s Story
story-3.excerpt: At 3 years old, Lyonichka’s life changed suddenly. A severe illness, later diagnosed as the rare West Nile virus, struck him without warning.

sections.heading: The onset of illness 💔
sections.body: At 3 years old, Lyonichka’s life changed suddenly. A severe illness, later diagnosed as the rare West Nile virus, struck him without warning. Within a short time, he lost the ability to move his arms and legs and could no longer breathe on his own — a ventilator became necessary to keep him alive.

sections.heading: The prognosis
sections.body: Doctors at several clinics delivered difficult news to Lyonichka’s mother: her son would never breathe or move independently again. Even after thorough examinations in Germany, the prognosis remained unfavorable.

sections.heading: Seeking help ❤️‍🩹
sections.body: Lyonichka’s family, supported by Olesia, the lead doctor, did not accept this prognosis. Olesia sent medical records to specialists worldwide, consulted with doctors, and explored treatment options in various countries. Her persistence led to the right choice: the ANAGENNISI clinic in Greece, where the GMTP team provided expert care for this complex case.

sections.heading: The road to recovery
sections.body: Through specialized treatment and surgery on his diaphragm, Lyonichka began to overcome the effects of the illness. Gradually, he regained movement in his arms and legs and — remarkably — began breathing without the ventilator.

sections.heading: Dreams for the future 💗
sections.body: Today, Lyonichka is learning new languages and dreams of becoming a blogger to inspire and help others. His journey continues, and his family remains committed to helping him thrive.

PrivacyPage.metaDescription: What data the foundation collects, how we use it, and how to ask us to delete it.
PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy

who.title: Who we are
who.body: Charitable Foundation "NEW LIFE!" (EDRPOU 42792589). For anything related to personal data, write to <email>support@newlife.foundation</email>.

data.title: What data we collect
data.body:
1. Through the "Become a volunteer" and "Become a partner" forms: name, email or phone, message text.
2. Through the request-for-help form: name, contact details, a description of the health condition and, optionally, medical documents. These requests often concern children — in that case they are submitted by parents or guardians.
We collect no other data and use no cookies, trackers, or analytics services.

health.title: Health data
health.body: Information about health conditions and medical documents is sensitive data. We process it solely to help find and arrange treatment. By submitting such information, you consent to its processing for this purpose.

storage.title: How data is transferred and stored
storage.body: Volunteer and partner forms are delivered via the Web3Forms service to our email. Help requests arrive at our email and in the foundation's internal Telegram channel. Only foundation staff have access to submissions.

sharing.title: Who we share data with
sharing.body: To arrange treatment, we may share patient information with medical institutions, including abroad — only to the extent needed to help, and with your consent. We do not share data for advertising or mailings, and we do not sell it.

retention.title: How long we keep data
retention.body: Help-request data is kept as long as needed to work on your case, and for some time after it concludes, then deleted. Volunteer and partner data is kept to stay in touch with you.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask us at any time to show, correct, or delete your data — write to <email>support@newlife.foundation</email>.
